# Larkspur Ferries: funding application (draft 3, extract)

## Q3. Benefit to residents

The service will create about 60 jobs across crewing, ticketing, maintenance and the terminal café.

## Q7. Safety certification

The operator holds a current passenger licence for its existing route. Certification of the new vessels is in hand.

## Q9. Governance

A project board of five meets every quarter. Its members bring experience of shipbuilding, finance and public transport.

## Q12. Passenger forecast

We expect 410,000 passengers in year two. The 2023 pier survey (300 respondents) and regional tourism growth of 4% a year support this.

## Q16. Capital budget

The capital budget for vessels is 8.1m, set at the outline stage.

## Q18. Match funding

Match funding of 2.4m is secured from three funders, listed in the table below.

## Q23. Fares

A single fare of 6.50 is affordable, well below the 14.00 charged for the harbour cruise.

## Q31. Staffing

Forty-two crew are needed at launch. A training partnership with the harbour college will supply them.

## Q40. Carbon saving

Each crossing replaces a car journey around the estuary, at the national average emissions figure.

## Q49. Fleet

The fleet will be two new vessels and, later, a third hull for winter cover.

## Q56. Supplier quote

The shipyard has quoted 9.2m for two vessels, fitted out and delivered.

## Q62. Terminal

We have a good relationship with the port authority, which owns the terminal.
